claims.text: The starting alloy is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
As-cast CoCrFeNiTi is a single-phase simple solid solution.
The as-cast state has coarse grains.
The as-cast state has low internal lattice strain and low defect density.
Coarse grains and low lattice strain or defect density permit facile dislocation glide.
Facile dislocation glide and limited grain-boundary strengthening govern the low hardness and strength of the as-cast alloy.
HEBM at approximately 400 rpm for 1–6 hours with a 20:1 ball-to-powder ratio, followed by SPS at 900–1000 °C for 10 minutes, produces a nanocrystalline and strained microstructure.
The processed alloy has a grain size below 48 nm.
The processed alloy forms a non-equilibrium mixed-phase structure containing approximately 83% FCC and 17% BCC.
Grain refinement increases strength and hardness through Hall–Petch grain-boundary strengthening.
Severe plastic deformation during milling increases dislocation density.
The increased dislocation density raises resistance to further deformation.
Solid-solution effects provide additional resistance to dislocation motion.
The HEBM-and-SPS-processed alloy will reach a Vickers hardness of approximately 675 HV.
The HEBM-and-SPS-processed alloy will reach a compressive strength of approximately 1894 MPa.
The processed alloy will exhibit intergranular fracture characteristics.
The increases in hardness and compressive strength will correlate with nanocrystalline grain structure and increased dislocation density.
Sintering above approximately 1000 °C may cause grain coarsening and invalidate the proposed strengthening response.
Excessive milling may cause phase decomposition or over-straining.

contradictions.description: The causal framing describes applying HEBM and SPS to an as-cast alloy, but the processing conditions specify nominally equimolar elemental powders. Comparing an as-cast bulk alloy against a specimen synthesized from elemental powders changes both precursor state and processing route, so it is not the same controlled intervention implied elsewhere.
